entrada.titulo: Secure and trusted data sharing in smart healthcare using blockchain and IoT integration

perfil_anterior.problema: Centralized storage architecture in most IoT healthcare systems can lead to a single point of failure and easy manipulation.
perfil_anterior.solucao: Blockchain with IoT integration can help healthcare systems overcome centralized communication architecture
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: The results show that public healthcare systems based on the Blockchain considerably boost efficiency and performance by integrating IPFS.
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Investigar a integração de identidade auto‑soberana (SSI) para controle de acesso pelos pacientes; aplicar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para compartilhamento granular de dados de saúde; testar a arquitetura em ambientes de cidades inteligentes com edge computing distribuído; explorar mecanismos de revogação cross‑organizacional usando credenciais verificáveis; avaliar a escalabilidade e latência da solução em cenários com milhares de dispositivos IoT; combinar blockchain com arquiteturas zero‑trust para reforçar a confiança entre organizações de saúde.

content identifier (CID), attached to them. CID links all the connected hashes to store 
the root hash, allowing the information chunks to be uniquely identified by their hash 
values. An open network like BitTorrent allows for the movement of files. In IPFS, the 
addresses of stored data are maintained in a DHT. IPFS uses a Merkle Tree structure to 
store the hash values of linked files. To improve healthcare systems’ speed, accessibility, 
storage capacity, and scalability, blockchain networks only save the file address rather 
than the entire file. The Blockchain network within healthcare organizations are linked 
to the IPFS similarly to how webpages are linked. IPFS keeps a local hash file for fre -
quently viewed files and enables rapid access to these files on subsequent tries. Anyone 
accessing the hash address can download a file via the IPFS distributed network [ 16]. In 
IPFS, once a file is uploaded, its hash is shared among all peer nodes in the network for 
instant access and to prevent data from having a single point of failure. Here, scalability, 
interoperability, and consistency issues are addressed with the IPFS, which also offers 
security and boosts the efficiency of healthcare systems.
1.1 Motivation
Although we cannot entirely eradicate every disease that affects people today, we can 
adopt innovative technology to reduce the severity of patients’ conditions and offer 
superior healthcare for a healthier world. Most past research focused on sensor-based 
healthcare systems to deliver remote healthcare services, improve patient cure rates, 
and eliminate the need for patients to travel to healthcare facilities. Still, the system’s 
privacy, scalability, security, and efficiency should have been addressed. In recent years, 
healthcare organizations have explored Blockchain integration with IoT to enable all IoT 
devices to interact without relying on trustworthy third parties. Blockchain technology 
has enabled healthcare businesses to effectively manage a growing number of distributed 
data transactions instead of traditional centralized ones. As more patients are added, the 
Blockchain healthcare system’s ability to connect, store, preserve, transact, and retrieve 
data becomes more challenging. This is because the system saves data in the Blockchain 
network. This framework integrates an IPFS with the Blockchain network to address the 
challenges of scalability, interoperability, efficiency, and security and improve storage 
capability.
1.2 Novel contributions
1. It presents a Blockchain-based novel framework to address healthcare systems’ data 
privacy, security, interoperability, scalability, and efficiency challenges.
2. It Integrates an Interplanetary File System (IPFS) with the Blockchain network to 
reduce blockchain network overload and enhance healthcare systems’ scalability and 
storage capacity.
3. It employs a device proxy to keep track of vulnerable devices and a cryptographic 
message authentication mechanism to keep data confidential.

resposta.resumo: O artigo propõe uma arquitetura que combina blockchain e IPFS para superar limitações de privacidade, escalabilidade, segurança e eficiência em sistemas de saúde IoT. Os dados são fragmentados, armazenados com identificadores criptográficos (CID) e distribuídos via rede P2P, evitando ponto único de falha. A integração reduz a sobrecarga da blockchain, melhora a capacidade de armazenamento e permite acesso rápido a arquivos frequentes, enquanto um proxy de dispositivos e autenticação criptográfica protegem a confidencialidade dos dados.

resposta.interpretacao: O texto descreve como a combinação de blockchain e IPFS pode eliminar o ponto único de falha ao distribuir dados de saúde, melhorar a escalabilidade ao armazenar apenas endereços na blockchain e acelerar o acesso via cache local, ao mesmo tempo que introduz mecanismos de autenticação para proteger a confidencialidade.
resposta.duvidas: Não há detalhes sobre métricas de desempenho, custos de implementação ou avaliação prática em larga escala; também falta informação sobre como a solução lida com a revogação de credenciais ou a interoperabilidade entre diferentes provedores de saúde.
